resources.string: A copy of everything in the app — tasks, notes, books, their covers — kept in your oursidecar account, so a lost phone loses nothing. Three made by hand and one made every week; only you see them.
Sign in to oursidecar to keep backups there.
Type the oursidecar password once, and this phone keeps backups there.
This phone was signed out of backups — on the web, or by the server. Sign in again to go on.
This oursidecar account does not keep backups.
By hand %1$d of %2$d · Weekly %3$d of %4$d · each up to %5$s
Everything in the app as it is now. It goes up in the background, and on after the app is closed.
Choose the backup the new one takes the place of. It is deleted only once the new one is whole on the server.
The backup of %1$s is deleted from oursidecar for good.
Everything in the app on this phone is replaced by the backup of %1$s. What is here now and not in it is lost.
The backup of %1$s was encrypted with the oursidecar password of that day. Type it.
This is not the password the backup was encrypted with.
Not chosen yet: nothing goes up until it is.

Encrypted on this phone with your oursidecar password: the server keeps only what it cannot read. If the password is forgotten and reset, these backups can no longer be restored. After the password is changed, older ones open with the old one.
Kept on the oursidecar server as they are: whoever has access to the server can read them.
Type your oursidecar password: the key is made from it on this phone and never leaves it.
A backup every week (Wi-Fi, while charging)
The backup is larger than the 200 MB oursidecar keeps.
What came down is not the backup the server listed. Nothing was changed.
The backup is no longer on the server.
Sign in to oursidecar again: the encryption key is not on this phone.
Choose whether to encrypt the backups first.
